pull_request.title: feat: implement contract_call_in_loop lint
pull_request.body:
Closes #16

## Summary

Adds a new lint, `contract_call_in_loop`, that flags cross-contract invocations made via `env.invoke_contract(...)` when the call site sits inside a `for`/`while`/`loop` body. Each cross-contract call spins up a new VM context and re-charges dispatch/instantiation overhead, so repeating it per iteration multiplies that cost and is almost always a sign of a missing batch endpoint on the callee, or a call whose result could be computed once and reused.

Default severity: `warn`.

## Implementation details

- New `CONTRACT_CALL_IN_LOOP` lint declared and registered in `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs`, alongside the existing lints, with category `LintCategory::Compute` in the `LINT_METADATA` registry.
- Detection follows the same structure as the existing loop-based lints (`SorobanStorageInLoop`, `HostInLoop`): resolve the method-call receiver's type, peel references, confirm it's `soroban_sdk::Env` via `match_soroban_def_path`, check the method name is `invoke_contract`, and confirm the call sits inside an enclosing loop via `enclosing_loop`/`get_enclosing_loop_or_multi_call_closure`.
- Unlike `unnecessary_host_function_call`, this lint does **not** gate on `depends_on_loop_state` — a cross-contract call is expensive on every iteration regardless of whether its arguments change, since the VM-instantiation cost is fixed per call, not per distinct input.
- Help text suggests either adding a bulk/batch endpoint on the callee contract, or hoisting the call out of the loop if its result is invariant.

## What is and isn't covered

**Covered:**
- `env.invoke_contract(...)` calls inside `for`, `while`, and `loop` bodies.
- Suppression via `#[allow(contract_call_in_loop)]`.

**Not covered (documented as follow-up in `docs/lints/contract_call_in_loop.md`):**
- `env.try_invoke_contract(...)` — the fallible counterpart is not yet matched.
- Generated contract clients (types produced by `contractimport!`/`contractclient!`, conventionally `*Client` structs) that wrap `invoke_contract` internally — e.g. `token_client.transfer(...)` inside a loop has the same cost profile but isn't detected yet. This requires recognizing generated client types by structural convention rather than a fixed def-path, which is left as a follow-up per the issue's suggested scope.

## Files changed

**New:**
- `docs/lints/contract_call_in_loop.md` — rule reference page with a batching example, "why is this bad", suggested fix, and a "deliberately not covered" section.

**Modified:**
- `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs` — lint declaration, `LateLintPass` impl, registration, `LINT_METADATA` entry.
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs` — added `invoke_contract` to the mock `soroban_sdk::Env` stub, plus new test fixtures.
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr` — updated expected UI-test output (new warnings + line-number shifts from the new fixtures).
- `docs/SUMMARY.md`, `docs/lints/README.md`, `docs/cost_rationale.md` — link/reference the new lint.
- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — feature list, example, `budget.toml` sample, and Unreleased changelog entry.

## Tests added

In `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs`:
- `bad_invoke_contract_in_for_loop` — `invoke_contract` inside a `for` loop → **flagged**.
- `bad_invoke_contract_in_while_loop` — inside a `while` loop → **flagged**.
- `bad_invoke_contract_in_loop_loop` — inside a `loop` → **flagged**.
- `good_invoke_contract_outside_loop` — single call outside any loop → **clean**.
- `allowed_invoke_contract_in_loop` — `#[allow(contract_call_in_loop)]` suppression → **clean**.

## How to test

```bash
# Install prerequisites if needed
cargo install cargo-dylint dylint-link --version "^6.0.1"

# From soroban_cost_lints/
cargo test ui

# Full workspace suite (unit + integration + UI tests)
cargo test --workspace

# Lint/format checks
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

All of the above pass locally.

feat: implement contract_call_in_loop lint

Adds a new lint that flags cross-contract invocations made via
env.invoke_contract(...) when the call site sits inside a for/while/loop
body. Each such call re-instantiates a VM context and re-charges dispatch
overhead, so repeating it per iteration is almost always a structural
design smell (missing batch endpoint on the callee, or a cacheable
result).

Follows the existing receiver-type-resolution + enclosing_loop pattern
used by soroban_storage_in_loop and host_in_loop. Client-struct detection
(contractimport!/contractclient! generated *Client types) and
try_invoke_contract are documented as follow-up work, not yet covered.

Refs #16

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' into feature/contract-call-in-loop-lint

# Conflicts:
#	CHANGELOG.md
#	README.md
#	docs/SUMMARY.md
#	soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr

fix: resolve CI build failures in SARIF output and fixture workspace

- SarifRun.results was typed Vec<SarifResult> while the SARIF result
  builder constructed plain serde_json::Value objects via json!(),
  a leftover mismatch from a prior merge that broke compilation.
  Retype results as Vec<serde_json::Value>, drop the now-dead typed
  Sarif* structs, and wire the already-collected rule descriptors
  into tool.driver.rules.
- integration.rs used HashSet<String> but inserted &str literals;
  fix the declared type.
- alpha/beta fixture crates each declared their own [workspace]
  while also being listed as members of the parent workspace,
  causing cargo metadata to fail with "multiple workspace roots
  found". Drop the redundant per-crate [workspace] tables.

These were the actual cause of the "SARIF result missing level"
CI failures reported on PRs #232, #267, #269, #270 (all inherited
the same broken merge state) — the binary failed to compile, it
was not a runtime field-mapping bug.
